content: The passage explains that as the size of input (e.g., number of elements to sort) increases, the running time of an algorithm increases as well. To analyze this, we express running time as a function of input size. Importantly, we typically seek upper bounds on running time—guaranteeing that the algorithm will not take longer than a certain amount of time. This provides a useful guarantee to users, especially in real-time systems, unlike lower bounds, which don’t ensure timely completion.
